A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to construct threshold and revocation cryptosystems via extractable hash proofs.

we present a new paradigm for constructing noninteractive cryptographic protocols, which is based on a new primitive called extractable hash proof systems, and which allows us to construct threshold and revocation cryptosystems that are more efficient and flexible than previous constructions, while at the same time, they provide a higher security level.

we show how the extractable hash proof technique, which has been used to construct threshold signature and encryption schemes based on RSA, can be used to construct similar threshold signature and encryption scheme based on factoring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that the notion of extractable hash proofs (a notion we introduce in the paper) can be used to obtain a variety of threshold and revocation cryptosystems.
the new framework provides a unified approach to construct threshold and revocation cryptosystems based solely on the existence of a hash function with certain properties.
